column1: # Hostname / URL keyword terms — the NETWORK-LAYER tier.
# This is the list the socket filter and Chrome's declarativeNetRequest consult.
# It closes the threat model's "New domain, registered today — Open in blocklist
# mode" row, and unlike the browser extension it works for every application on
# ║  READ THIS BEFORE ADDING A LINE                                           ║
# ║  A wrong verdict here takes out an ENTIRE SITE, not one page. That makes  ║
# ║  this the highest-blast-radius file in the repo. `kind` is the whole      ║
# ║    token      the term must equal a complete hostname label token         ║
# ║               (split on . - _ and a trailing digit run). Safe for short   ║
# ║    substring  matches anywhere in the hostname. ONLY for strings you have ║
# ║               verified appear inside no innocent word, in any language    ║
# ║               we serve. The compiler refuses substring terms under 4      ║
# ║               characters, but that floor is not a substitute for actually ║
# ║  Every `token` line below that could have been `substring` carries the    ║
# ║  reason it is not. Those reasons are load-bearing — they are the sites    ║
# ║  that stay reachable. `never_keyword.txt` is the second net under this    ║
# No innocent English or transliterated-Arabic word contains any of these.
# Each line names what it would have broken as a substring.
# ^ essex.gov.uk, sussex.ac.uk, middlesex.edu, wessex.nhs.uk, sexton, sextant
# ^ too short to be meaningful anywhere; also matches version strings
# ^ class, assets, assist, passage, embassy, massachusetts
# ^ title, institute, constitution, competition, attitude, entity
# ^ Ford Escort, escort carrier, police escort — a legitimate word in three
# The digit-for-letter forms are short by nature, so almost all of them are
# token-only. This tier is what makes the mechanism work for Arabic hostnames
# at all — see terms.ar-latn.tsv for why.
# ^ CRITICAL: tasks, asks, desks, risks, masks, kiosks. As a substring this one
#   term alone would block a large fraction of the web.
# ^ jinsiya (nationality) — the hostname twin of the الجنسية text trap
# Side doors: the sites people move to when the big ones are blocked. Brand
# names with no innocent reading are substrings, so a mirror on a new domain
# (fansly-free.net, thothub-new.org) is caught; `coomer` is also a surname
# (coomerlaw.com) and `nsfw` starts the names of moderation libraries
# (nsfwjs.com), so both must be a whole label.
